thread.text: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites, which had brought him down thither.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 9:9
precepts.why:
“the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man.” His master saw that the Lord was with him and made him overseer over his house, and “the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake.” And “Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured”: he had a very good reputation, and people looked at him as a man of integrity and good character.

Then his master’s wife “cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.” He refused: his master had committed all that he had to his hand, “neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?” Nobody was watching him. He could have done it, but he said no. That is where integrity comes from: making the right decision when nobody is watching.

Ecclesiasticus 9:9 gives the same wisdom as a command: “Sit not at all with another man’s wife, nor sit down with her in thine arms, and spend not thy money with her at the wine; lest thine heart incline unto her, and so through thy desire thou fall into destruction.” Do not sit with another man’s wife at all. Do not play with it. Do not be drinking around somebody else’s wife, because your heart will incline to her, and both of you will destroy everything.

Joseph lived that. When “there was none of the men of the house there within,” she caught him by his garment, “and he left his garment in her hand, and fled.” He knew it was wickedness that would destroy his reputation and everything he had worked so hard for, and that he would not only be sinning against her but against the Lord. He fled rather than sit with it, even though he went to prison when she lied on him.

precepts.label: Isaiah 41:14
precepts.why:
The Bible says God is a man of war. War is coming to this place; God is bringing war to the earth. And we should not be afraid of it. Isaiah 41: “For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee. Fear not, thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel; I will help thee, saith the Lord, and thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel”. God is talking to us. Don't be afraid; he is going to help us.

Read on: “Behold, I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth: thou shalt thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and shalt make the hills as chaff”. A new sharp threshing instrument is a weapon, a weapon of war. The mountains are the nations, and we are going to beat them small. “Thou shalt fan them, and the wind shall carry them away, and the whirlwind shall scatter them”. A time is coming when we will say, there was a place named America; what happened to it? It will be wiped out and never remembered again.

So when war comes, we should be celebrating, happy, not sad, because through those wars our salvation and our freedom come. We should pray for that thing. Our job now is to prepare for it, spiritually and mentally, not physically: prepare ourselves and our people, and keep a food pantry, as Bishop has been teaching for a while.

That preparing is spiritual warfare: “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh”; the weapons of our warfare are “mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds”. Don't get caught up in the foolishness of this place, the marches and the stupidity, even with your own family. Stay in the scripture, cast down every evil imagination in the minds of our people, and bring every thought “to the obedience of Christ”, the black Messiah. The man of war fights for us.

precepts.label: Numbers 30:3-5
precepts.why:
Numbers 30:6-8 is about your prayers, sisters, and the power the Most High gave the husband over the wife. If the husband hears her vow and holds his peace, “then her vows shall stand”; but if he disallows her the day he hears it, “he shall make her vow which she vowed, and that which she uttered with her lips, wherewith she bound her soul, of none effect: and the Lord shall forgive her.” Some of you will go to the Most High praying against your husband, and he can say, Lord, do not listen to that trash.

Keep reading back in the chapter and it speaks of the father, for those of you who do not have a husband. It starts with the man: “If a man vow a vow unto the Lord, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word”.

Then: “If a woman also vow a vow unto the Lord, and bind herself by a bond, being in her father’s house in her youth”. Being where? In her father’s house. “And her father hear her vow, and her bond wherewith she hath bound her soul, and her father shall hold his peace at her: then all her vows shall stand”.

“But if her father disallow her in the day that he heareth; not any of her vows, or of her bonds wherewith she hath bound her soul, shall stand: and the Lord shall forgive her, because her father disallowed her.”

So God also gave the father power over the daughter. The same power the husband has over the wife’s vow, the father has over his daughter’s vow while she is in his house. That is the order the Most High set, and nobody made it up: do not get mad at us, we are reading the Bible.

Yet there are negroes online, some elders from other camps, certain unsavory Black Hebrew Israelite camps, saying that Moses left the truth, that he was off and didn't have the spirit. What are you talking about? It says right there in verse 17: “only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses.” The Lord was with Moses. Shame on you for not reading the scriptures, and shame on the men that follow you.

Because Sirach says, “Make not thyself an underling to a foolish man; neither accept the person of the mighty.” Camps like that have made themselves students and underlings to a negro that's just as dumb as they are.

Israel followed Joshua because they had seen Moses' character in him while he ministered under Moses. The company you keep matters. Put yourself under a foolish man, and you learn his folly instead.

precepts.label: 2 Kings 21:16
precepts.why:
Kings tells the same account in its own way. It had already said Manasseh “hath done wickedly above all that the Amorites did, which were before him, and hath made Judah also to sin with his idols.” He went above the Amorites; Manasseh was a monster. Chronicles gives more of the detail: he “caused his children to pass through the fire”, ancient abortions, burning his babies alive; he observed times, used enchantments and witchcraft, dealt with a familiar spirit and with wizards; he was a sorcerer. And he put an idol in the temple.

Then Kings adds what Chronicles leaves out: “Moreover Manasseh shed innocent blood very much, till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another.” Babies on babies. That is a lot of blood, from one end of Jerusalem to the other. And it was not only him: the people did the same thing, for this was “beside his sin wherewith he made Judah to sin, in doing that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.”

Manasseh was behind a lot of death, sorcery and witchcraft; he did evil way beyond worthy of death. He killed babies, he went into witchcraft, he defiled the temple. And yet, when he was in affliction and humbled himself greatly, the Lord forgave Manasseh, heard his supplication, and put him back on the throne. The Lord has mercy on whom he will have mercy.

That is why it is so important for us to learn humility. People fall, and the Most High is able to raise them up again, like David. But don't abuse it. All of us in here ain't David; don't think, I can do what David did. No, negro, you ain't David. You're not Manasseh. You ain't Moses. The Lord puts it there to remind us that the graces and mercies of Christ were around back then too, from time to time. Don't get stupid and get prideful. Humility.

precepts.label: 1 Esdras 5:73
precepts.why:
“Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity builded the temple unto the Lord God of Israel”, these heathen, placed in the land in the time of Assyria, came and said, “Let us build with you: for we seek your God, as ye do”. We want to serve God, we want to be around you, we want to cleave. But at that time we were back from exile and not ruling; we were under Persian subjugation.

1 Esdras gives the answer: “It is not for us and you to build together an house unto the Lord our God. We ourselves alone will build unto the Lord of Israel”. We ourselves alone. We don't need your help. Our forefathers understood that in captivity solidarity and unity were paramount. Yet today, as this truth grows and is harder to blackball, there are Israelites with a house negro spirit trying to find a place in our salvation for our enemies, whose heaven is our hell. That is post-traumatic slave disorder, and it is pushing the same agenda into the truth.

Because they were told no, “the heathen of the land lying heavy upon the inhabitants of Judea, and holding them strait, hindered their building”. You know how Esau gets when he is told no: he turns into a different beast. It is the same when black folks built for themselves: Black Wall Street, Rosewood, Tulsa, Seneca Village, Black Bottom in Detroit, Lake Lanier. Whenever we build, they come along wanting in, and then destroy it.

“And by their secret plots, and popular persuasions and commotions, they hindered the finishing of the building”. Secret plots are the laws they passed: redlining, blackballing, Jim Crow, systematic laws to make sure black folks don't thrive again, because left to ourselves we rebuild. Segregation was the best thing for us; integration in captivity destroyed us. Popular persuasions today are Christianity, social media, politics, philosophies, New Year's Eve, Christmas, Halloween, Easter, Islam, money, podcasters and content creators.

“so they were hindered from building for the space of two years, until the reign of Darius.” Their plan was never to join us. If they really believed in helping, why go through all this to stop the building? Their plan was to join, infiltrate and destroy from the inside, like the Black Panthers: first the feminist and lesbian black women were let in, and a feminist-minded black woman is the white man with breasts and melanin, the white man's drone; then the white folks came in, and it was a wrap. Martin King found at the end that he had integrated his people into a burning house. That is why our fathers said, we ourselves alone will build.

The pattern holds in our history: in exile in Europe we taught Esau our laws, and he destroyed us and became us; in Africa we taught the Arab, and he enslaved us. When you are in exile, you do not share your wisdom with the nations. The time is to keep the commandments of God and the faith of his Son, gain favour with our God, and get out of this condition, then deal with the nations after that.

precepts.label: Isaiah 35:3-4
precepts.why:
David prays, “raise me up, that I may requite them”: raise me up the third day, so I can get vengeance on the traitor who ate of my bread. Isaiah tells the faithful to hold on for that vengeance: “Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.”

In every IUIC school some brothers may be weak and feeble, spiritually. Build them up. You have to build your inner circle up, loyal and faithful brothers who know the scriptures and fear God, and then have a circle outside of that of trustworthy, loyal men, so that when Jacob's trouble comes you don't all fall.

“Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not”. Brothers and sisters, be strong, because at times you might get afraid, but the Lord has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.

Then: “behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you.” We must believe that our God will come with vengeance. A recompence is a requital, the same word as “that I may requite them” in the psalm: an appropriate return for wrongdoing.

Isaiah 47 shows that vengeance on Babylon: “Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen”. All these fake Christians talking about America being a Christian society: their nakedness is uncovered by the word of God, and all their shameful deeds are revealed. “I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.” Christ is not coming back meeting them as a man. So strengthen the weak, fear not, and wait on the God who comes with recompence to save us.

“For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it.” It was not the enemy that set David up, or he would have been ready, because he knows who the enemy is. “But it was thou, a man mine equal, my guide, and mine acquaintance. We took sweet counsel together, and walked unto the house of God in company.” It was the man he trusted, the man he went fishing with, and that took him by surprise. Later in the same psalm David describes that man: “The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.”

A man mine equal: an officer of ten, of twenty, of fifty, just like me. We took sweet counsel together: Deacon, I need counsel; Captain, what do you think about this? But while he was taking counsel, he was plotting. Some are plotting to take your wife: she is too beautiful for him. Some are plotting to take your position at the job you brought them into, telling the white man, give me his position. I picked him up every Sabbath and every Wednesday, and when he came to betray me he had no problem doing it.

“Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.” Christ was betrayed that way: “Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?” Today we do not kiss, but we dap: Shalom, Captain, Most High bless. That smooth greeting can be the betrayal. In 2018 a man who sat in another man's house, barbecued and travelled with him, came and took all his furniture and put his children to sleep on the cold floor.

Jeremiah warns: “Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.” Supplant means betray, plot. Other camps slander our members and leadership, because they know our people believe anything without proof; they are Esau in black skin, who “have taught their tongue to speak lies.” They come asking to fellowship, but we are not stupid.

It was not the enemy that killed Thomas Sankara; it was his best friend, who grew up with him. It was Maduro's own handpicked bodyguards who stood down and handed him over, taking American money instead of a bullet for him. That is war in the heart behind smooth words. David is telling you: do not fall asleep.

precepts.label: Psalms 74:18
precepts.why:
The psalm ends its first cry with, “O God, how long shall the adversary reproach? shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever?” How does the enemy blaspheme? By making our signs their signs. White Jesus is blasphemy. White angels are blasphemy. All these whitewashed images are blasphemy; it is evil.

Further down Asaph says it again: “Remember this, that the enemy hath reproached, O Lord, and that the foolish people have blasphemed thy name.” The foolish people are the nations, primarily, and in some instances our own people too.

To blaspheme is to speak evil of his name, his reputation. White Jesus is blasphemy. He died for all people, the gospel is for all people, all nations can be saved: blasphemy. He isn't the son of God, he doesn't exist, I'm an atheist, evolution: blasphemy. His name is blasphemed every day all around the world.

That is why the enemy is not only the one who burned the sanctuary and the synagogues, as Babylon and Assyria did. The enemy is also the one who keeps reproaching God's name by painting over his people, so that “We see not our signs.” We don't see statues of David or Solomon or Christ as black men; we see their images, their depictions.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 3:48
precepts.why:
The psalm says of the enemy, “they set up their ensigns for signs.” What are their ensigns for signs? Cesare Borgia; Mother Mary, white Mary; baby white Jesus; white prophets; the Last Supper; the Sistine Chapel. Posing themselves as God, as the prophets, as the angels, as the heavenly Father: whitewashing our ensigns and making our ensigns their signs.

Maccabees shows it was done before: they “laid open the book of the law, wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images.” The book of the law is our Bible, and the heathen sought to paint the likeness of their own images into it.

They made our signs their signs. The Greeks did it, the Romans did it, Spain did it, Portugal did it, Britain did it, the Dutch, the French: they all did it, and they still do it. It was blasphemy back then, and it is blasphemy now.

That is why Asaph cries, “We see not our signs.” The heathen painted themselves into the book of the law, and our people no longer see their own images in the scriptures that were written about them.

precepts.label: Luke 22:48
precepts.why:
“Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.” The last part is the point: the kisses of an enemy are deceitful. And Luke shows the kiss: “Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?” Judas betrayed Christ with a kiss. The man betrayed him with the very sign of love.

Today we do not greet each other with a kiss like that, but we have our own greeting: Shalom, Captain, Most High bless. That is the betrayal. The embrace, the salute, the Shalom, and then the knife. That is the kiss of an enemy.

We saw it in 2018. A man who had been in another man’s house, greeting him with Shalom, barbecuing together, traveling together, came to that same man’s house, took all his furniture and put his children on the cold floor to sleep. He did not care. Not only did he betray the man, he betrayed all his children.

There is nothing worse than a traitor. And some of you think once you betray your brother or your sister, that is the end of it. It is not. The one who betrays with a kiss will be dealt with too. That is why the kisses of an enemy are called deceitful: Judas is the pattern of the familiar hand that destroys.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 16:14
precepts.why:
“For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God.” That is America going into space; America was the first there, and America invented the airplane that ascends “above the heights of the clouds.” “I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north.” That is the Monroe Doctrine, now the Donroe Doctrine. The congregation is Mexico, Central and South America, Panama, Puerto Rico, Dominica, Jamaica, Trinidad and the Caribbean islands, where the twelve tribes of Israel are. America, the king of Babylon, the oppressor, sits upon the congregation and rules over us: fall in line, or what we did to Maduro we will do to you. And it is in the sides of the north, North America; that is why its treaty with Europe is called the North Atlantic Treaty.

Jeremiah shows where Israel is: “Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt; But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north.” The land of the north is North America. It is going to be said that the Lord brought the children of Israel out of this side of the world.

“and from all the lands whither he had driven them: and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.” Israel is in North America and all through this hemisphere, and 2 Esdras speaks of the ten tribes coming to this side of the world.

So the one who sits on the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north is sitting on Israel. According to prophecy, America will be sitting on these congregations in the last days, during the fourth seal, and bad things are about to happen on this side of the world. But the Lord will bring his people up out of the land of the north.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 15:28-45
precepts.why:
Isaiah sees “the burden of the desert of the sea”: “the treacherous dealer dealeth treacherously, and the spoiler spoileth.” That is America, which invites you to a peace talk and then bombs your country, as it did Iran, and now tells every nation to take the deal: only white folks can have nuclear weapons, no weapons for you brown people. “Go up, O Elam: besiege, O Media”: Iran, Pakistan, India, that whole section. Right now they are in a sighing period, bases destroyed and generals killed by drones, building up their arsenal and waiting. Then the burden upon Arabia, the sons of Ishmael, and “all the glory of Kedar shall fail.” Ezra shows how it all comes together.

“Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the east: Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots.” Turkey, which is part of NATO, is making a defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a NATO of the Arab nations, because Erdogan hates the Israelis so much. When Israel bombed Qatar, the Muslim world called an emergency summit, and Saudi Arabia called for revenge. “Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood, and with great power shall they come, and join battle with them, and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.” The Carmanians are Iran, joining the Arabs, and the land of the Assyrians here is the Israelis.

“And then shall the dragons have the upper hand, remembering their nature.” Right now the Arabs are kissing America's butt, but they will remember their nature. Genesis 16 gives it: Ishmael “will be a wild man; his hand will be against every man, and every man’s hand against him; and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren.” Wild enough to run into a crowded room with C4 strapped to his chest for 72 virgins. His hand against every man means you have no friends among them: they are true nationalists, and all twelve princes dwell together through that region.

It is only Black people that are not nationalists. We love everybody, we have to be friends with everybody, and meanwhile we are put to death left and right. Stop being stupid, men. A nationalist loves his nation and his people; that is the greatest commandment, love God and love your brother. Every nation loves its own. Christ was a nationalist: I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. And now Ibrahim Traoré is uniting Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso, the most docile nations; the spirit of life is coming into them through the brothers teaching and preaching in Africa.

“And if they shall turn themselves, conspiring together in great power to persecute them, Then these shall be troubled” … “and shall flee. And from the land of the Assyrians shall the enemy besiege them, and consume some of them.” All the Arab nations conspiring together against the Israelis, just as we saw in the clip.

“Behold clouds from the east and from the north unto the south” … “full of wrath and storm.” The east is Asia, China and North Korea; the north is Russia, Turkey and Europe; the south is the Arabs and Africa; the clouds are their ships. “They shall smite down a great multitude of stars upon the earth, even their own star”: missiles, like the ones the Iron Dome shoots down. “And blood shall be from the sword unto the belly, And dung of men unto the camel’s hough.” Then “great storms from the south, and from the north, and another part from the west”: the west is America and Canada.

Then “they shall pour out over every high and eminent place an horrible star.” That is different from the stars before: the horrible star is the ICBM. With it, “Fire, and hail, and flying swords”, the conventional missiles. “And they shall go stedfastly unto Babylon, and make her afraid” … “then shall the dust and smoke go up unto the heaven, and all they that be about her shall bewail her”, like the kings of the earth in Revelation 18 standing afar off, crying that in one hour her judgment is come. Ezra 15:60 even shows them returning to Babylon that was destroyed: the air force and navy still fighting from a base that is gone.

That is what Isaiah's watchman saw: “Babylon is fallen, is fallen; and all the graven images of her gods he hath broken unto the ground.” Fallen twice, because the Israelis over there fall too. Cesare Borgia, Santa Claus, the Thanksgiving turkey, the Easter bunny, the Greek statues everywhere: all of it finished. It is Bible prophecy unfolding before our eyes, and while it happens, get yourselves together, brothers and sisters.

precepts.label: Psalms 118:22
precepts.why:
“they are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink. For the Lord hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep, and hath closed your eyes: the prophets and your rulers, the seers hath he covered.” Covered what? Their eyes. They were evil and rebellious back then, and evil and rebellious now.

David shows who they rejected: “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” The builders are the rulers: the elders, the Pharisees, the scribes, whose eyes the Lord covered in darkness because they were wicked as hell. The stone they refused is Christ.

That is why Christ could ask them, “What is this then that is written, The stone which the builders rejected”: he was speaking the parable against them. The husbandmen beat the servants and killed the heir, and the rulers knew he was talking about them. They were drunk, but not with wine; their eyes were darkened, and so the builders refused the head stone of the corner, the black Messiah.

precepts.label: Psalms 69:22
precepts.why:
The Lord closed the eyes of the rulers, and David prays it over them: “Let their table become a snare before them: and that which should have been for their welfare, let it become a trap.” The table is the Bible. Let the Bible be a trap and a snare for the wicked of my people.

“Let their eyes be darkened, that they see not; and make their loins continually to shake.” That is the elders, the leaders, the rulers. Their minds are lost: they read the Bible and cannot understand what they are reading, because they are too rebellious and evil.

“Pour out thine indignation upon them, and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them. Let their habitation be desolate; and let none dwell in their tents.” Why? “For they persecute him whom thou hast smitten; and they talk to the grief of those whom thou hast wounded.” That is Christ: they spoke evil of him whom God smote and wounded.

That is Isaiah 29: drunken, but not with wine; the spirit of deep sleep poured out on them; the prophets, rulers and seers covered. The very book that should have been for their welfare became their snare.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 36:16
precepts.why:
Why did the Lord cover the eyes of the prophets and rulers? “But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and misused his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy.”

Ezra says the same: “I sent unto you my servants the prophets, whom ye have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands”. We tortured our prophets, killed them, and tore them in pieces.

Stephen told the rulers of his time, “as your fathers did, so do ye. Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and they have slain them which shewed before of the coming of the Just One”. The Pharisees and the builders of that time were the children of the murderers of the prophets who prophesied of Christ. Their fathers killed the prophets who spoke of him, and then they were born and killed Christ himself. They have always hated him, from their fathers to them. When Stephen reminded them, “they were cut to the heart”, because they knew, and they gnashed on him and killed him.

So the darkness of Isaiah 29 did not fall without cause. They mocked, despised and misused, until there was no remedy, and the Lord poured out on them the spirit of deep sleep.

To our brothers and sisters in Venezuela: repent. You cannot stop the white man; let him do what he was supposed to do. The evil in the city is the Lord’s counsel standing, and it is revealed to his prophets.

You are a man, but if you want I will make you a woman; I can fix that, I made that happen. America is the land of entitlement and privilege. precepts.why:
Isaiah 59 ends with the Lord seeing “that there was no man”, no intercessor, so his own arm brought salvation: Christ “put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing.” “The Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob”: not all nations. And his covenant is his spirit upon us and his words in our mouth, and in our children's mouths, and our children's children's, for ever. Wisdom of Solomon shows what that Redeemer brings.

“But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High.” There is no death to the righteous. If you are in this truth keeping the commandments in the faith of Christ, you live forever; our brothers and sisters whose bodies returned to the dust, those spirits are coming back. We have to believe that.

“Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the Lord’s hand.” The glorious kingdom shall be on earth: that is New Jerusalem. The crown is the one in 2 Esdras 2:42-45: we are going to get crowned with power. “For with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.”

“He shall take to him his jealousy for complete armour”: Christ is coming back for war. “And make the creature his weapon for the revenge of his enemies”: that leviathan is going to come out and attack those bastards on the navy. “He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate”, the same as we read in Isaiah 59, “and true judgment instead of an helmet. He shall take holiness for an invincible shield. His severe wrath shall he sharpen for a sword, and the world shall fight with him against the unwise.”

“Then shall the right aiming thunderbolts go abroad; and from the clouds, as from a well drawn bow, shall they fly to the mark.” Those weapons won't miss; that lightning won't miss. “And hailstones full of wrath shall be cast as out of a stone bow”, like in the time of Joshua, “and the water of the sea shall rage against them”, tsunamis, “and the floods shall cruelly drown them. Yea, a mighty wind shall stand up against them, and like a storm shall blow them away: thus iniquity shall lay waste the whole earth, and ill dealing shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty.”

That is what we are waiting for: the second coming of Christ. And God would not be just to let the nations off the hook; if he punished his own people, America, England, Japan and Australia will not be unpunished. So while we wait, we must be preparing our hearts, our minds and our souls.

“My people hath been lost sheep: their shepherds have caused them to go astray, they have turned them away on the mountains: they have gone from mountain to hill, they have forgotten their restingplace.” The shepherds, the pastors, lead our people from one religion to another, and they have forgotten their restingplace, the word of God. Christ told them a parable: “No man putteth a piece of a new garment upon an old; if otherwise, then both the new maketh a rent, and the piece that was taken out of the new agreeth not with the old.” Christ is the piece of new garment; the new covenant was being ushered in and they were not ready for it. “And no man putteth new wine into old bottles; else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles shall perish. But new wine must be put into new bottles; and both are preserved.” The new wine is the new covenant in Christ. The new bottles are us being born again: new creatures, new men, new women.

“No man also having drunk old wine straightway desireth new: for he saith, The old is better.” That is how the Pharisees and scribes felt about Christ's teaching, and so it is today with Christians and the true teaching of Christ and the Israelites. Our people like their old ways and old traditions, and when we bring them the new covenant in Christ by keeping the commandments, they say, I don't want that. So “their adversaries said, We offend not, because they have sinned against the Lord, the habitation of justice, even the Lord, the hope of their fathers.”

precepts.why:
Jeremiah 50 ends with the hammer of the whole earth broken: “Therefore hear ye the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Babylon; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”. The least of the flock is the so-called Israelis, that tiny speck in the midst of the brown and black nations. They bomb Qatar during peace talks, cry help us, and America comes to their rescue. “surely he shall make their habitation desolate with them”: America desolate, and little Israel over there wiped out too. “At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth is moved, and the cry is heard among the nations.”

Then chapter 51 turns to us: “For Israel hath not been forsaken, nor Judah of his God, of the Lord of hosts”. That means us. That is Simon: a friend only in name, a companion turned into an enemy. Because of one argument, he told the heathen about all the money in Jerusalem.

And that money was not his to give away. The treasury held what the law set aside: the tithe for the Levites, who had no inheritance, and for the stranger, the fatherless and the widow, so that the Lord might bless the work of their hands. So he was ready to see the Greeks take what belonged to the widows and orphans rather than let Onias have the last word. This is a no good dude: from brother to betrayer.

thread.label: 2 Maccabees 3:7-40
thread.text: Now when Apollonius came to the king, and had shewed him of the money whereof he was told, the king chose out Heliodorus his treasurer, and sent him with a commandment to bring him the foresaid money.

classes.title: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.label: Acts 6:1-6
precepts.why:
The high priest Onias told Heliodorus “that there was such money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children.” The temple had money in it for the widows. So how come, in the days of the apostles, “there arose a murmuring of the Grecians against the Hebrews, because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration”? Why didn’t they just get it from the temple?

Because these were followers of Christ, and the priesthood had already agreed to cast out any man who confessed him. The widows of the disciples were getting nothing from the temple because they believed in Christ.

So the twelve said, “It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables.” To serve tables means to take care of the widows, the orphans and all of that. “Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business. But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word.”

This is how the deacons were chosen. “And the saying pleased the whole multitude: and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch.” Stephen, the one we always read about, was one of the first deacons chosen. They set them before the apostles, “and when they had prayed, they laid their hands on them.”

So the care of widows and the fatherless has always been a sacred charge among our people, kept in the temple in Onias’s day and put into the deacons’ hands in the apostles’ day. That is what Simon betrayed to the Greeks.

precepts.label: John 9:22
precepts.why:
The temple kept money “laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children”, yet in Acts 6 the widows of the disciples were neglected in the daily ministration. Why couldn’t they get it from the temple? John shows what the priesthood had already decided.

The man born blind was healed, and his parents would not answer plainly: “These words spake his parents, because they feared the Jews: for the Jews had agreed already, that if any man did confess that he was Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.”

They were kicking people out left and right. So Peter and them saw that the widows were not getting anything from the temple, because they believed in Christ. Put out of the synagogue, they were cut off from the relief the temple held for widows and the fatherless.

That is why the apostles had to look out seven men of honest report to serve tables and take care of the widows themselves. And that is how the deacons came to be chosen.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 3:8-12
precepts.why:
The apostles said, look out “seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom”, to take care of the widows. You may ask, what did they base choosing these men on? Timothy shows how they gauged it.

“Likewise must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre; Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience. And let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless.”

Then: “Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things. Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well.” You didn’t just look at the man; you looked at his wife too. Sometimes you find a brother who appears decent, but his wife is ratchet, low down, no damn good. That’s a reflection on you, brother. If your wife is low down and no good, you ain’t guiding her right.

So they looked at the man, then they looked at the wife, and said, he has wisdom, he is of honest report, and they chose seven. The ones trusted with what belongs to the widows and the fatherless had to be proved and blameless, the very opposite of a man like Simon, a betrayer of the money.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 5:3-16
precepts.why:
The money in the temple was “laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children.” What is a widow? You may say, a sister whose husband died. But Paul says, “Honour widows that are widows indeed.”

First, “if any widow have children or nephews, let them learn first to shew piety at home, and to requite their parents.” Then: “Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day.” A widow had a duty. “But she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth”, because the widows made a kind of vow to dedicate themselves to the Lord and pray night and day for the benefit of Israel. And “if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel”: the family looks after her first and foremost.

“Let not a widow be taken into the number under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man.” There was a widowhood of sisters whose job was to pray for Israel, fasting and praying night and day. She didn’t just sit around and say, my husband died, I’m a widow. She had an obligation. She had to be sixty, married to one man in her life, “Well reported of for good works”: she raised children, lodged strangers, the brothers who came to the city, washed the saints’ feet, relieved the afflicted.

“But the younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry.” Wanton means lustful. She gave up the vow to pray and fast night and day because she wanted a man. “Having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith.” That widowhood was not taken lightly. And they learn to be idle, “wandering about from house to house”, tattlers and busybodies. So “I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house”: get a husband, sister.

“If any man or woman that believeth have widows, let them relieve them, and let not the church be charged; that it may relieve them that are widows indeed.” You, her son, her daughter, her uncle, her brother, take care of her, so the church can care for the real widows who have no family. That is who the money Simon betrayed was for.

precepts.label: Luke 2:36-37
precepts.why:
Paul says a widow indeed “trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day.” Luke gives an example of exactly that.

“And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser: she was of a great age, and had lived with an husband seven years from her virginity; And she was a widow of about fourscore and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day.”

She did not depart from the temple. She served God with fastings and prayers, night and day. That is what widows did. She was married to one man, well over threescore years old, and she gave her life to prayer for Israel.

Those were the widows the temple money was laid up to relieve in Onias’s day: sisters who had dedicated themselves to the Lord. To betray that money to the Greeks was to take the bread from women like Anna.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 34:21-22
precepts.why:
Onias said there was money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children, “and not as that wicked Simon had misinformed”, and that it was “altogether impossible that such wrongs should be done unto them, that had committed it to the holiness of the place.”

There is a scripture that says keeping a man’s earnings from him is like murder: “The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood. He that taketh away his neighbour’s living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.”

What Simon did was no light thing. Taking money from the widows, the orphans, the fatherless and the strangers is murder. That was their livelihood; we took care of them with that money. Simon would rather have Esau come and take it all than help his own people. He is a murderer.

That is why it is never just one sin. All I did was tell them about the money? No, you did worse than you think. Sin is a domino effect: one hits the next and it goes all around. That is why Onias was in such agony, the priests lay on their faces before the altar and the whole city cried to heaven, and why the Lord of spirits sent the horse with the terrible rider and the two young men to scourge Heliodorus.

thread.label: 2 Maccabees 4:1-3
thread.text: This Simon now, of whom we spake afore, having been a betrayer of the money, and of his country, slandered Onias, as if he had terrified Heliodorus, and been the worker of these evils.

classes.title: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.label: Proverbs 29:24
precepts.why:
“This Simon now, of whom we spake afore, having been a betrayer of the money, and of his country, slandered Onias”. Simon of the tribe of Benjamin revealed the secret of the money to the Greeks and then slandered Onias the third, telling them Onias was the one who did that to Heliodorus. This Simon was no damn good.

Now look at the ones who stand next to that kind of man: “Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth it not.”

The type of man who is a partner with it hates his own soul. He hears the cursing and does not tell it. He keeps it tucked in. That goes directly against the law in Leviticus 5, where the one who hears and does not utter it bears the iniquity.

So it is not only the Simon who is guilty. The one who stands by, hears the evil, and keeps quiet is partnered with him, and he is hating his own soul.

precepts.label: Leviticus 5:1
precepts.why:
“And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.”

What does that mean? Whatever the judgment is on that man, you get the judgment. This is why in the hood, in the ghetto, people see murders all the time and say, I’m not saying nothing. Then weeks later, a month, a year, that same person ends up dead, and you say, what did she do, they never killed nobody. No: they were a witness, and they chose not to utter it.

Read on and the law also says “if a soul swear, pronouncing with his lips to do evil, or to do good, whatsoever it be that a man shall pronounce with an oath, and it be hid from him; when he knoweth of it, then he shall be guilty in one of these.” And when he is guilty, “he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing”.

A story from camp: the brothers were planning who to take traveling, and one brother’s hair was unkempt. He was told to trim it, and he answered, well, I guess I’m not traveling then. A couple of men heard it. A young man from Detroit told what was said, and when the officer who heard it first was questioned the next week, he said, I heard it, I was going to tell you next week. Fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me.

Be mindful of brothers. They may seem decent on the outside, but you have to be mindful of the things they say, or don’t say.

precepts.label: Psalms 31:13
precepts.why:
Simon slandered Onias the third. So how serious is slander? “For I have heard the slander of many: fear was on every side: while they took counsel together against me, they devised to take away my life.”

Slander is not a light thing. It is the first step of a counsel against a man’s life. The ones who slander take counsel together, and what they devise is to take away his life.

That is exactly the road Simon walked. He slandered Onias to the Greeks, and it did not stop at words: “when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon’s faction murders were committed”. The slander of many leads to the taking of life.

precepts.label: Psalms 101:5
precepts.why:
“Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off: him that hath an high look and a proud heart will not I suffer.”

There is a lot of slander in the Israelite community; Deacon Asaf has been going over it in classes these last two weeks. There are camps that thrive off slander, hatred, name calling, ridicule and false accusations.

God already told you he is going to cut off people who do that. Cut off means he is going to kill them. So for you to join with these people, you are nothing but a fool.

And the high look and the proud heart come from the slander; that is what they do. They think God is with them, and the men and women around them, as stupid as they are, believe God is with them. God is not with them, not according to these scriptures.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 9:4-5
precepts.why:
“Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.”

Every neighbour will walk with slanders. “And they will deceive every one his neighbour, and will not speak the truth: they have taught their tongue to speak lies, and weary themselves to commit iniquity.”

There are people who love the slander. They teach their tongue to speak lies, and they are very good at it; there are some very good liars out there. You ever see a woman caught in the midst of adultery? She starts crying: this is not what it looks like. And some men will dismiss what they saw with their own eyes. Some of you are such a simp.

Don’t bring anybody like that around. They cannot roll with us. Let them stay over there with those other camps. That is what Simon was: a brother that supplanted, walked with slanders, and would not speak the truth about Onias.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 26:5-7
precepts.why:
“There be three things that mine heart feareth; and for the fourth I was sore afraid: the slander of a city, the gathering together of an unruly multitude, and a false accusation: all these are worse than death.”

Simon did all three. The slander of a city: God does not like that thing, and Simon slandered the city. The gathering together of an unruly multitude: Simon had all the Greeks gather together to try to get the money from Jerusalem. And a false accusation: he accused Onias of doing this to Heliodorus. God said all these are worse than death.

Then think about this: don’t tell me what they say about me, tell me why they feel so comfortable telling you. In every school there is that one brother or sister that all the murmurers draw to, and they tell them all the things they don’t like about people. Why do they draw to you? You obviously did not have our back, because they are slandering and they feel so comfortable saying evil to you.

A deacon once pointed out a sister in red shoes with high heels and called her a hoe because of the shoes. The Bishop called Deacon Asaf, Deacon Malachi and the others over and asked them if she was; they said no. And he blew that brother’s spot up in front of them. You cannot come to me with evil. We must train ourselves to hate evil.

precepts.label: Exodus 20:16
precepts.why:
Simon “was he bold to call him a traitor, that had deserved well of the city, and tendered his own nation, and was so zealous of the laws.” He was so bold he called Onias the high priest a traitor, that type of a brother, a man zealous of the law.

The law is plain: “Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.” Don’t bear false witness.

These are basic laws, but for some reason in the black community they are so difficult. Just so, so difficult. Simon broke this one outright when he falsely accused Onias before the Greeks, and everything that followed came out of that false witness.

precepts.label: Proverbs 25:18
precepts.why:
“A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.”

Why is he a maul, a sword and a sharp arrow? Because that man will get people hurt, and will get people killed. A false witness is a weapon.

That is what Simon’s false witness against Onias became. He called the high priest a traitor, and before long “by one of Simon’s faction murders were committed”. His lie was a sword in the hands of his faction, and it drew blood among his own people.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 7:13
precepts.why:
“Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good.”

Use not to make any manner of lie, not a big one and not a small one. The custom of it is not good: when lying becomes your custom, it becomes what you are.

This follows the false witness of Exodus 20:16 and the maul, sword and sharp arrow of Proverbs 25:18. Simon made a custom of lying: he betrayed the money, slandered Onias, and called a man zealous of the law a traitor. These are basic laws, and our people must keep them.

precepts.label: James 4:1-3
precepts.why:
“But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon’s faction murders were committed”. Simon hated Onias the third so much that he had one of his men kill one of Onias’s priests. That is why it is never just one thing; it is a domino effect of sins. James shows where it comes from.

“From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members? Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain”. Simon wanted the upper hand over Onias, and he could not get it. So what did he do?

“ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not.” Because you are not praying to the Lord about it. “Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.” When you pray and still do not receive, it is because you ask for the wrong reasons. You have a lustful purpose behind it, a purpose that is not for the benefit of the nation.

This is a self-examination class for all of us: these are the attributes of Simon.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:21-22
precepts.why:
“Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment: But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment”.

It does not start with the murder. It starts with anger at your brother without a cause. “and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council”. Raca means thou fool, vain fellow, and the council there is man’s council.

“but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.” Just continuing the sin, the name calling and all of that, puts you in danger of hell fire. That is when God has to step in.

These are the attributes of Simon, and the class is a self-examination for all of us. Simon’s anger toward Onias turned into slander and name calling, calling him a traitor, and it ended in murder.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:15
precepts.why:
“Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.”

That is Simon. He hated Onias, his brother, and his faction committed murders. This is the domino effect: it starts off as coveting; Simon coveted power. From there it turned to anger, from there to slander, and from there to murder. It is never just one sin, and not only are you affected, the people you sinned against are affected too.

Holding on to anger is like drinking poison and expecting the other person to die. You are drinking poison waiting for somebody else to drop dead, and they are not dropping dead. The only one being affected is you. This goes for men and women.

Onias was the opposite. He went to the king “not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all, both publick and private”. He did not even go there to accuse Simon. That is the difference between a brother and a betrayer.

thread.label: 2 Maccabees 4:1
thread.text: This Simon now, of whom we spake afore, having been a betrayer of the money, and of his country, slandered Onias, as if he had terrified Heliodorus, and been the worker of these evils.

classes.title: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 10:20
precepts.why:
Simon was “a betrayer of the money, and of his country”, and he slandered Onias, the righteous high priest, trying to get him taken out to replace him. After him came Jason, Onias’s own brother, another house negro, who labored underhand to be high priest; and then Menelaus, Simon’s brother, who outbid Jason for the priesthood. Simon, Jason, Menelaus: all traitors of their own people.

The betrayal for money did not stop with them. When Maccabeus and his men “ran with violence upon the strong holds of the Idumeans”, they killed no fewer than twenty thousand, and about nine thousand fled into two very strong castles. Maccabeus left Simon, Joseph and Zaccheus to besiege them and went where he was needed more.

“Now they that were with Simon, being led with covetousness, were persuaded for money through certain of those that were in the castle, and took seventy thousand drachms, and let some of them escape.” The enemy in the castle bribed them: let us escape and we will pay you. They took the money and let them go.

When Maccabeus heard it, he “accused those men, that they had sold their brethren for money, and set their enemies free to fight against them.” They sold out their own brothers. “So he slew those that were found traitors, and immediately took the two castles.” That is what was done to traitors back then: they got death.

So from Simon slandering Onias to the men selling their brethren for seventy thousand drachms, it is the same spirit. All skinfolk ain’t kinfolk. There were always those among us making a covenant with hell and death for money and the white man’s favor, even until now.

thread.label: 2 Maccabees 4:4-6
thread.text: Onias seeing the danger of this contention, and that Apollonius, as being the governor of Celosyria and Phenice, did rage, and increase Simon’s malice,

classes.title: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 11:21
precepts.why:
Simon hated Onias so much that one of his faction murdered one of Onias’s priests, and he got Apollonius, the governor of Coelosyria and Phenice, to rage and “increase Simon’s malice.” Not only did he turn his own group against the high priest; he went to the other nations against him. That is how far your anger goes when you cannot get your way.

That spirit shows up again in 1 Maccabees: “Then came ungodly persons, who hated their own people, went unto the king, and told him that Jonathan besieged the tower.” You will always have that: certain ungodly men and women among us who hate their own people and run to the king.

See how it relates to us today. On the Carmelo Anthony verdict, one black commentator celebrated the guilty verdict and blamed the family for spending the money raised for his defense on houses. Another said he was overjoyed there were no black people on the jury. Whatever happened to a jury of your peers? It is the same thing they did back then: a whole white jury, and a judge who allowed it, with connections to the other family. Whatever the white man did, not guilty; a black man on trial, three or four minutes, guilty.

Then a black woman called black supremacy the most dangerous ideology in the world and said every race is tired of black people, and “we” want y’all gone. Where does black supremacy exist? Nobody has ever seen it. And she is not the only one who thinks like that. There are brothers and sisters calling themselves repented Israelites who think exactly like that; we had a bunch of them leave in 2018.

Onias went to the king “not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all.” The ungodly who hate their own people go to the king to accuse them. That is the difference between Onias and Simon.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:1-2
precepts.why:
Onias went to the king “not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all, both publick and private.” Simon was full of malice, envy and evil speaking. Peter tells us what to do with all of that.

“Wherefore laying aside all malice”: when you give yourself to the Lord, one of the first things you must do in repenting is lay aside all malice. “And all guile”: guile means deceit; put it away from you. “And hypocrisies”: don’t be a hypocrite. “And envies”: whatever envies, hatreds and jealousies you have, put them from you. “And all evil speakings.”

“As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.” You cast those sins away and start all over again as newborn babes, desiring the commandments in Christ. That is the only way you can grow in this truth.

If you apply verses 1 and 2, everyone will see a substantial change in your life. But if you are the same grimy brother or sister from last year and the year before that, we know you have not been applying 1 Peter 2:1-2. Our people forget history quickly; we cannot afford to become Simon.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:9
precepts.why:
Onias the high priest went to the king “not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all, both publick and private.” He did not even go there to accuse Simon. That shows the character of Onias III, a great and upstanding elder man.

Christ says, “Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.” That is the attribute of Onias. His own people had turned on him, Simon had one of his priests murdered, and the governor was raging against him, and still he went seeking the good of all, public and private, not revenge.

That is what a child of God does. Simon’s spirit lusts, envies, slanders and kills to get the upper hand. The peacemaker seeks the good of the whole nation.

precepts.label: Romans 12:18
precepts.why:
Onias sought peace, going to the king seeking the good of all rather than to accuse his countrymen. That is one of his attributes, and Paul gives the rule: “If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.”

Notice the words: if it be possible. As much as lies in you, you live peaceably. But it is not always possible. Onias “saw that it was impossible that the state should continue quiet, and Simon leave his folly, unless the king did look thereunto.” Simon was causing insurrections in Jerusalem, and Onias wanted the king to look into it.

Blessed are the peacemakers, and live peaceably if at all possible, but peace doesn’t always work with some people. Some spirits are grimy, and at the end of the day they don’t want peace with you. They want you dead. Onias did everything that lay in him; the rest he took to the king.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:14
precepts.why:
Onias’s attributes are the attributes of a man of God. He went to the king “not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all.” Hebrews tells us to walk the same way: “Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord.”

Follow peace with all men, and holiness with it. Without them no man shall see the Lord. You cannot see the Lord walking in Simon’s spirit of malice, slander and murder.

Onias followed peace and holiness even when his friend Simon turned on him, and soon after his own blood brother Jason labored underhand to take the priesthood from him. Put yourself in his sandals. He still sought peace, until he saw it was impossible for the state to stay quiet and Simon to leave his folly unless the king looked into it.

precepts.label: 2 Thessalonians 3:1-2
precepts.why:
Onias saw “that it was impossible that the state should continue quiet, and Simon leave his folly, unless the king did look thereunto.” We read, blessed are the peacemakers, and if it be possible, live peaceably with all men. But peace doesn’t always work with some people.

Paul says: “Finally, brethren, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may have free course, and be glorified, even as it is with you: And that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked men: for all men have not faith.” Meditate on that. Some men you cannot reason with. There is no, let’s sit down and talk, let’s get two witnesses. Some spirits are grimy. At the end of the day they don’t want peace with you; they want you dead.

There are Israelite camps like that. Brothers were at an event, and one of these camps was walking by; a brother said shalom to one of their men, and he cursed him out for it. These are unreasonable and wicked men.

They have no faith, and here is how we know: they are teaching now that Moses is in a lake of fire, and that John the Baptist was a wicked Israelite. Blasphemous new doctrines. They are filled with hatred, and they are unreasonable. We pray to be delivered from them, just as Onias could not make peace with Simon and had to take it to the king.

thread.label: 2 Maccabees 4:7-17
thread.text: But after the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus, called Epiphanes, took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest,

classes.title: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 7:4-5
precepts.why:
“Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest.” This is Onias III’s own blood brother. Not only does Onias have to deal with Simon of the tribe of Benjamin; now his brother is trying to take the priesthood from him. When problems come, they come. Put yourself in his sandals: his good friend Simon turned on him, and now his own brother.

Sirach speaks to it: “Seek not of the Lord preeminence, neither of the king the seat of honour.” Why go there? The priesthood fell to Onias III; that was his lot. His brother said, I want it, I should have it, not my brother.

“justify not thyself before the Lord; and boast not of thy wisdom before the king.” Jason went to the king to get what the Lord had not given him, seeking preeminence and the seat of honour, and he bought it.

Sometimes it is not good enough for a brother to be the support brother. Onias was the high priest, and his brother should have supported him. Jason said, I think I can do a better job, and have access to all that money. You have to look at a man’s motives.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:5
precepts.why:
Jason undermined his own brother to become high priest. All of this ties into us today. “And if a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully.” You want to be an officer, a captain, a deacon, a bishop; you want to be moved up. You are not crowned except you strive lawfully.

Just as Jason undermined his brother, we have had brothers in here do the same thing. A brother said, we keep failing the officer of 50 test; I’ll get a copy with the answers and disseminate it. You might think, oh, it’s just cheating. No. It is worse than that. The officers of 50 counsel people. Now you have a brother who couldn’t pass it, who cheated and became an officer of 50, and he is counseling marriages. Y’all don’t see nothing wrong with that?

He is not qualified for that rank yet. The captains and deacons spend time on the exam, with variations on it, to see each man’s level of understanding, and a lot of it is counseling questions. The counselors mostly come from married men, and counsel must be accurate, on point and scriptural, not from your heart.

That is striving unlawfully, the same as Jason buying the priesthood. And a man who strives that way is not crowned.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 4:8
precepts.why:
Paul said a man is not crowned “except he strive lawfully.” What does he mean by crowned? He tells it in the same book: “Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.”

The crown is not a rank a man buys or cheats his way into, like Jason bribing the king for the high priesthood. It is a crown of righteousness laid up by the Lord, the righteous judge, and given at that day to those who strove lawfully and love his appearing.

So the brother who wants to be moved up, to be an officer, a captain, a deacon, must remember whose crown he is striving for. Jason got the rule in his hand for a time, but the writer of Maccabees still calls him “that ungodly wretch, and no high priest.”

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:43-47
precepts.why:
Who is it that gives out the crowns? Ezra saw it: “And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted; which I marvelled at greatly.”

Christ is a young man. He was crucified at 33, so art department, don’t make him look old. And taller than all the rest doesn’t mean by a couple of inches; it means by feet. You are going to know, that’s the Son of God right there, no question.

“So I asked the angel, and said, Sir, what are these? He answered and said unto me, These be they that have put off the mortal clothing, and put on the immortal, and have confessed the name of God: now are they crowned, and receive palms.” This is what we all want.

“Then said I unto the angel, What young person is it that crowneth them, and giveth them palms in their hands? So he answered and said unto me, It is the Son of God, whom they have confessed in the world. Then began I greatly to commend them that stood so stiffly for the name of the Lord.”

The crown comes from Christ, to those who confessed him and stood stiffly for the name of the Lord. It cannot be bought from a king the way Jason bought the priesthood, or cheated for the way a brother cheated the officer of 50 test.

precepts.label: Amos 5:12
precepts.why:
Jason promised the king “by intercession three hundred and threescore talents of silver, and of another revenue eighty talents.” What is that called? Bribery. He tried to bribe his way to become high priest. He paid money for an office that goes through bloodline.

Amos shows what the Lord thinks of it: “For I know your manifold transgressions and your mighty sins: they afflict the just, they take a bribe, and they turn aside the poor in the gate from their right.”

That is what they were doing back then. They take a bribe, they afflict the just, and the poor are turned aside from their right. Jason paid the bribe, the king took it, and Onias, the just high priest, was pushed out. The Lord knows those manifold transgressions and mighty sins.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 40:12
precepts.why:
Jason bought the high priesthood with bribes, and three years later he got a taste of it himself: Menelaus, Simon’s brother, offered the king three hundred talents of silver more than Jason and “got the priesthood to himself.” Jason, who had undermined his own brother, was undermined by another and had to flee into the country of the Ammonites.

Sirach says: “All bribery and injustice shall be blotted out: but true dealing shall endure for ever.” The Most High deals with bribes. Here comes Jason, the brother of Onias the high priest, trying to bribe his way in, and it is blotted out.

Sometimes it is not good enough for a brother to be the support brother. Onias was high priest and his brother should have supported him, but Jason said, I can do a better job, plus have access to all that money. Look at a man’s motives. Bribery does not last; true dealing endures for ever.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 12:1-2
precepts.why:
Jason “forthwith brought his own nation to Greekish fashion.” He built a place of exercise, brought the chief young men under his subjection and made them wear a hat, the hat of Hermes. “Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners.” This is when we became Greek citizens, and we worshiped idols.

That is why Paul says: “Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I would not have you ignorant. Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.” That goes back to what we just read. We were led by Jason into heathenish manners and carried away unto dumb idols.

Everything Paul writes is referenced in the histories. Paul didn’t just make stuff up; it was based on something. Where in the Bible do we find it? In the book of Maccabees, which Esau conveniently took out, so our people in Christianity are lost and confused.

All you men that teach on the street must know this history. Verses 10 to 16 sum up what Paul constantly referenced when he said there is neither Jew nor Greek: we followed the Greeks’ customs so earnestly and desired to be like them in all things.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 9:9-12
precepts.why:
“For it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of God.” Sometimes we take God’s laws for granted with the mentality, I can sin and God won’t do nothing. Ezra shows otherwise: “Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways: and they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments.”

“For such as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me.” Look at Jason Whitlock. In the interview he said he is not oppressed because he makes ten million dollars a year. That is a benefit. A lot of our people become doctors and make big money and say, if I can do it, you can do it, and they do not know God. Whitlock once posted Revelation 3:9 on his Instagram with no commentary, all Amalek attacked him, and he quickly deleted it. These people need a wake-up call.

“And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it.” They had liberty, because the brothers are out there teaching and the videos are in their feed. They see it, and they hate it.

“The same must know it after death by pain.” So who says that when you die you don’t get punished? You are going to know pain after you die, when Christ returns. Nobody escapes. That is why it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of God, as Jason did.
